land.text: Jeju Island, which Taejong of Joseon 'placed under firm central control' in 1404

successors.note: The page: 'the kingdom maintained local autonomy until 1404, when Taejong of Joseon placed it under firm central control and brought the Tamna kingdom to an end'; in 1402 the last lord, Go Bong-rye, 'voluntarily relinquished his title of seongju to the king and received a governor position'.

capitals.name: Jejuseong (Jeju City)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Mugeunseong [ko] (early); Jejuseong [ko] (later)'. The page gives no years or coordinates; the coordinate is Jeju City's.

keyframe_review.note: The Tamna page gives no area. Cliopatria's 1,959 km2 island outline is kept for 263..681. The page has 'no discovered historical record of the founding or early history of Tamna'; 'The first historical reference to the kingdom may come in the 3rd century CE, in the chronicle ... called the Sanguozhi' (the basis for Cliopatria's 263). 476: tributary of Baekje (page text; infobox 498-660); 662: tributary of Silla (infobox).

correction.text: the Cliopatria 263 island outline for 682..935 (years added)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 682..935: Cliopatria has no Tamna shape and folds the island into Unified Silla (that row's bbox reaches 33.20N). The infobox has Tamna a 'Tributary state of Silla (662–925)' and 'Independent state (?–498, 925–938)'; 'Tamna briefly reclaimed its independence after the fall of Silla in 935'. The island is kept as Tamna's own tributary state, to be tinted by the Silla dossier.

Same island outline 936..1271. 'it was subjugated by the Goryeo dynasty in 938, and officially annexed in 1105'; infobox 'Vassal state of Goryeo (938–1105)', then 'Local autonomous administration of Goryeo (1105–1275, 1301–1392)'. Cliopatria's Goryeo row does not include the island (its bbox stops at 34.29N).

Same outline 1272..1278. Infobox 'Local autonomous administration of Yuan dynasty as Tamna Prefecture (1275–1301)'; 'the Sambyeolcho Rebellion ... came to a bloody end on Jeju Island in 1274'. Cliopatria ends the row in 1278.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1272 island outline for 1279..1404 (years added)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1279..1404: Cliopatria ends Tamna in 1278 and the island is in nobody's row until Joseon (1395); the page has the kingdom 'maintained local autonomy until 1404' (infobox 'Local autonomous administration of Joseon (1392–1404)'). The island outline is kept as Tamna's, tinted by the suzerain dossiers (Yuan to 1301, Goryeo, Joseon).

ledger.note: 263: Tamna enters the map as the Jeju Island kingdom. The page has no founding date: 'no discovered historical record of the founding or early history of Tamna'; the legend puts the founders 'in the 24th century BCE' and 'The first historical reference to the kingdom may come in the 3rd century CE'. 263 is Cliopatria's first year.

ledger.note: 1404: Taejong of Joseon ends the Tamna kingdom. 'Taejong of Joseon placed it under firm central control and brought the Tamna kingdom to an end' (infobox 'Fall: 1404'); in 1402 the last lord Go Bong-rye 'voluntarily relinquished his title of seongju to the king'.

wars.name: Sambyeolcho Rebellion

zones.text: Jeju Island, where the rebellion 'came to a bloody end ... in 1274'

wars.outcome: The rebellion 'came to a bloody end on Jeju Island in 1274'; the island then ran as Tamna Prefecture under the Yuan, 1275 to 1301.
wars.note: The page gives no start year for the rebellion and no belligerents; the Goryeo and Yuan entries are the researcher's reading of the Yuan-era infobox lines. Zone: Jeju Island, where the fighting ended (page); added by reviewer jk-02-b.

certainty.note: The island's coast is a natural limit, but Tamna's political status moved between independence, tribute and local autonomy (infobox: independent ?-498 and 925-938, tributary or vassal at other times) and the pages give no territorial frontier events; drawn soft.

notes:
Is the Cliopatria row (263..1278) successive states? No: the Tamna page describes one kingdom on Jeju Island from its first record to 1404 whose status changed (infobox: 'Independent state (?–498, 925–938)', 'Tributary state of Baekje (498–660)', 'Tributary state of Silla (662–925)', 'Vassal state of Goryeo (938–1105)', 'Local autonomous administration of Goryeo (1105–1275, 1301–1392)', 'Local autonomous administration of Yuan dynasty as Tamna Prefecture (1275–1301)', 'Local autonomous administration of Joseon (1392–1404)'). The text puts the Baekje tribute in 476 and the infobox in 498. So one dossier, no split. The Cliopatria gaps 682..935 (island inside Unified Silla's shape) and 1279..1394 are filled with new keyframes, and the end is moved from 1278 to 1404.
Suzerain relations are recorded in the suzerains' dossiers, as the vassal_start/vassal_end schema asks: Baekje (476 to 660, written here in baekje.json); Silla 662 to 925 (the Silla and Unified Silla dossiers, jk-02-a), Goryeo 938 to 1105 and 1105 to 1275, 1301 to 1392 (Goryeo group), Yuan 1275 to 1301 (Yuan group), Joseon 1392 to 1404. The Tamna page's 1105 'officially annexed' is not drawn as a loss of the island, because the same page says local autonomy continued; the Goryeo dossier should decide between a vassal tint and direct rule. The Unified Silla shape 682..935 contains Jeju (bbox 33.20N); its dossier should subtract it if Tamna is drawn as a tributary state.
Only two dated territorial events exist on the page (263 first reference, 1404 end); capital years are not given (the capital entry is one span with Jeju City's coordinate). The second page opened (Jeju Island) had no History section and gave nothing.
No rulers: the Tamna page lists a legendary king table (Go Eulna 2337-2206 BCE) that is not a documented list.
